clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old male presented with a painless, gradually enlarging swelling of the right side of his face since childhood, reaching approximately fist-size by presentation. Clinical examination revealed a soft, fluctuant, compressible extraoral swelling extending from the right outer canthus to the mandibular border and from the right corner of the mouth to the pre-tragus region, with slight temperature elevation and jaw deviation to the left on closing. Intraorally, bluish-red discoloration was noted in the posterior right buccal mucosa extending to the right soft palate, with a soft, compressible, non-tender lesion demonstrating pulsation and elevation to a red-purplish appearance on palpation. Panoramic and submentovertex radiographs demonstrated multiple concentric calcifications in the soft tissue shadow suggestive of phleboliths. Based on these clinical and radiographic findings, the diagnosis of hemangioma was established using conventional radiography. The benign nature of the disease was confirmed, and the patient was referred to the department of interventional radiology for definitive management.
